# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

insights.line: What made the others more pressing?

whys.g1: Both answers say the schedule and subs not showing up is what pushes the log down the list, so one plainly named group about keeping the schedule and getting subs on site is exactly how a super would sort them.
whys.g2: There is no junk, explicit or off-topic answer on this line, so nothing junk is in the group.

founder.order_why: The window question (screen 4) sits between two halves of the same context step (screens 3 and 5), so I left the context, picked a recall window, then came back to it. Settling where the idea applies first and then asking how far back to look would read straighter.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 carry the identical question 'Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies.', so it reads as the same context screen asked twice.
founder.missing: Nothing in the flow asks about my solution, my price or my buyer: the narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew and pushed to Procore/ACC; about $1k per site per month; and the general contractor paying rather than the superintendent. The study stops at the problem. The problem itself is also narrowed to 'sorted site photos by hand', when my problem is the hours spent writing the whole daily log in the trailer after the site walks.

PRIMARY.order_why: Asking which part of the log I'd most like made easier before asking how typing up the last log actually went feels backwards, since walking me through that day first would make the pick easier.
PRIMARY.missing: How long the daily log actually took me (the hours I spend uploading photos into Procore after the walk), and whether I've had to pull old logs and photos to back myself up in a delay dispute with the owner.

screens.why1: Right after I said how supers get the log done today, it makes sense to check the scale of how that went before the problem part closes.
screens.why2: Walk, trailer, typed up and written up that day are exactly how supers talk about the daily log.
screens.why3: Any super knows how long the log took after the last walk and whether it got done that day.
screens.why4: The rungs are distinct steps on time, but 'Took a couple of hours after the walk' and 'Took the rest of the evening' can blur for a super who knocks off late, and the super who fills the log in as they go during the day has to squeeze into 'within half an hour of the walk'.
screens.why5: It keeps what I typed (the hour in the trailer and the evening lost to it), and the rungs show nothing of Fresco, videos or the contractor who pays.
screens.why7: Every rung is on the one measure of time after the walk, there are five from working to never done, the line sits under the working first rung so the belief can hold or fail, the bar names that rung word for word, and the escape belongs to the stranger's item, not this screen.
screens.instead: Done as I went, finished by end of day · Took about an hour in the trailer · Took a couple of hours after the walk · Ran past three hours into the evening · Never got written up that day

screens.why1: Choosing who asks my questions belongs right before the link goes out to superintendents, after the problem has been set.
screens.why2: Two names with a five-second listen each, and the hint says plainly what it costs and how the link is sent.
screens.why3: I can play both clips and judge which one a super would hear over a generator and not hang up on.
screens.why4: Two distinct voices, each with a preview and a preselected default; no escape chip is needed for a pick like this.
screens.why5: It doesn't leak anything about Fresco, but the hint only talks about the voice while what I picked says it locks and records a face too, so I can't tell from the screen what gets recorded.
screens.instead: Who should ask construction superintendents your questions? (Daphne ▶ / Saskia ▶), with the hint saying Keel records the face and voice you pick once for 400 credits.

screens.why1: Right after picking who asks the questions, choosing how my supers will answer is the obvious next step before sending.
screens.why2: Plain words: talk to a video interviewer, read and tap, or let them pick; I'd answer on first read.
screens.why3: I know my supers are in a trailer at day's end with a phone, so I can judge whether they'd rather tap or talk.
screens.why4: The three options cover the real choices, are distinct, and 'Let them choose' acts as the fitting middle ground; no escape is needed for a setup choice.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product or roles leaks, and my pick 'Read and tap' sits cleanly as one of the options.

screens.why1: Once I've said how superintendents should answer, the obvious last step is deciding who gets the link, and that's how I'd recruit: the supes I met driving around Napa and the South Bay, by name.
screens.why2: Each option reads plainly on first pass; the only wobble is the second option switching from 'I' to 'you send them', which doesn't slow me down.
screens.why3: I know exactly who I have contact with and how I'd reach them, so this is mine to answer.
screens.why4: By name, a Keel contacts list and one open link for a group cover the real ways I'd reach supers, and they don't overlap.
screens.why5: My pick, people I know by name, each with their own link, is kept as I typed it, and nothing about Fresco leaks into the options.
screens.instead: Which construction superintendents get a link? (People I know by name, each with their own link / People I found with Keel on the Contacts page, one link each, I send them / A group, one open link I post where supers already are, each signs in with Google)

screens.why_b1: The verdict *Too few to call* sits under the title with the deciding number beside it (Frequency: 4 counted), and the Frequency card shows that 5 were needed.
screens.why_b2: Each card shows its count against its bar (6 of 7 at the bar; 4 counted, 5 needed), but the kicker's *4 TO 7 COUNTED* made me look twice, and this page never says why 3 of my 7 superintendents were not counted on three beliefs.
screens.why_b3: The statement is mine and I can recognise the beliefs, but *sort site photos by hand for the log* is Keel's phrasing, not mine (I said uploading photos and typing logs), and the Importance belief's *have five things that are hard* is clumsy wording I would not use.
screens.why_b4: *5 needed to call it* implies I need more answers, but the page never says so outright, and it says nothing about what the Prevalence hold means for the idea.
screens.why_b5: The n of 7 is visible throughout, the hold is called only *Holding up* and *at the bar*, and the beliefs with 4 counted are not called at all, so nothing claims more than the data supports.
screens.instead: Too few to call: on three of the four beliefs only 4 of my 7 superintendents counted (5 needed) because [reason]; get one or two more supers to answer before reading Frequency, Importance and Current solution, though nearly all did hand-log photos last week (6 of 7).

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Holding up' sits right beside '6 of 7 said yes · bar 6 of 7 · at the bar', so I see both the call and the number that decides it.
screens.why_b2: The strip shows 6 for and 1 against across 7 people, with my bar marked at 6 on a 0 to 7 axis, so what is counted, over how many and where the bar sits are plain at once.
screens.why_b3: I recognise my problem, but my segment's qualifier 'on commercial jobs' is dropped, and 'sorted site photos by hand' is a rewording of my uploading-and-logging pain that hints at another way of doing it.
screens.why_b4: 'Common among these 7, at your bar exactly' plus a pointer to the next two cards tells me to read on, but not what this means for Fresco or that the result sits on a knife edge.
screens.why_b5: n=7 stays visible, the small group is flagged as 'a lean, not a call', and the belief is only said to be holding, not strong.
screens.instead: At least 8 in 10 superintendents on commercial jobs: 6 of 7 said yes, exactly at your bar, so one more No would drop it below. Treat the problem as common but unproven, and let Frequency and Importance decide.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know exactly why there's no call yet.
screens.why_b2: Working days out of 5 and the median at 5 read at once, but the chart itself doesn't show it's over 4 people, and 'your bar · 4 of 5' sits so close to my '4 to 5 working days' that I had to read it twice to see it means people, not days.
screens.why_b3: Frequency and 'sort site photos by hand for the log on 4 to 5 working days out of 5' are my belief and my range, in a superintendent's words, though tagging a five-day count with '— the most recent time it happened' is odd.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic; it doesn't tell me that one more superintendent's count settles it, or that all four so far are at 4 or 5 days.
screens.why_b5: No claim goes past the data: n is shown, the small group is called 'a lean, not a call', and Hank and Luis are named as not counted with the reason.
screens.instead: All 4 counted put it at 4 or 5 of the last 5 working days (middle answer 5) — one more counted superintendent and this calls; 4 of 5 at your low holds it.

screens.why_b1: The status *Too few to call* sits right beside its number, *4 counted · 5 needed to call it*, so I know where I stand and why.
screens.why_b2: The bars count picks (8), but the strip and its *4 of 5* bar count people. Only 4 are counted, so I had to look twice to see which count the bar applies to.
screens.why_b3: I recognise *Logging the day's photos and notes* as mine. But the belief line mostly repeats my circumstance (*photos and notes still have to go into the daily log*), so it reads close to a tautology. The prompt also says *your last daily log*, not the site walk I'd now expect.
screens.why_b4: *Nothing is settled here yet* is a generic line. It doesn't tell me that 2 of my 4 supers put the schedule and subs ahead of the log, or what I need to get next.
screens.why_b5: The n is plain and *a lean, not a call* is honest. But the single empty cell suggests one more answer could settle it, and at 5 people it cannot hold: two are already against, so the best is 3 of 5 against a bar of 4. The screen never says which way it leans.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 2 of 4 put the log in their two, and Denise and Ray put the schedule and subs first. Even a fifth yes can't reach 4 of 5, so this is leaning against. Ask more supers whether the log beats the schedule and the subs for them.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 counted, 5 needed to call it', so I know the verdict and the number behind it.
screens.why_b2: The rungs and their counts read cleanly, but the strip's 'your bar, 4 of 5' with a ghost cell and the marker at 4 took me a second look, since only 3 counted for me and I had to work out that 4 of 5 is the bar's need, not my tally.
screens.why_b3: The act 'typing up the daily log after the site walk' and the rungs from 'Typed up within half an hour of the walk' to 'Never got written up that day' are my own words, and the belief line follows from them.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic; it does not say that 3 of the 4 counted already fell short, or that one more superintendent landing below the line would let this be called.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (6 answered, 4 counted), the two not counted are named with reasons, and 'a small group: a lean, not a call' keeps the 3-of-4 lean from being read as a held belief.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of the 4 counted took an hour or more after the walk, 1 was done within half an hour; one more counted answer and this can be called, so get one more superintendent through the study.

screens.why_b1: The verdict *Too few to call* sits right above *4 counted · 5 needed to call it*, so I know it isn't decided and exactly why.
screens.why_b3: Importance, with my circumstance (site walks done, photos and notes still to go into the daily log) and my job of logging photos and notes as one of the two worst, is the belief I checked, in my words.
screens.why_b4: Nothing tells me what to do with this: no 'get one more superintendent to answer', and no word on what the two againsts mean for pitching the log as the pain.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (4 counted, 2 against, 2 asked why here), the low n is said outright, and the one theme claims only its own 2.
screens.why_b6: Ray's 'the log can wait till morning, the deck can't' and Denise's log done on the tablet before the gate tell me the log is deferrable rather than urgent, which I hadn't put in my belief, even though the theme label just echoes the two options they picked.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 of 5 needed; one more superintendent's answer decides it. Both againsts say the log can wait while schedule and subs can't, so lead with time saved after the walk rather than the log as the worst pain.

screens.why1: As the first screen it rightly checks whether my jobs are on Procore or ACC before asking about my daily logs, since the rest only matters if they are.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are what every GC super I know says, and 'the jobs you're running now' is how I'd put it, even though I mostly run one job at a time.
screens.why3: I know exactly what platform my job is on because I'm in it every day uploading photos and logs.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it cleanly for a gate, and no escape chip is right since there's nothing to guess.
screens.why5: It only names the platforms the founder's segment names and says nothing about any product or what's coming.
screens.why6: Short and easy to hear once, though 'I'll read 2 options' before a plain yes-or-no is a bit stiff next to the guidelines' simpler 'Yes or no.'
screens.instead: Do any of the jobs you're running now run on Procore or ACC? Yes or no.

screens.why1: Right after confirming I'm on Procore or ACC, asking whether I hit the photo chore this week is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: I'd answer it, but 'sort' isn't how I'd put it: I upload, tag and caption photos into the log, so 'sort' makes me pause over whether it means folders, tagging or picking which ones go in.
screens.why3: Whether I spent time going through my own walk photos for the daily log this week is something I know cold.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it and don't overlap, and the chips belong to the story box after a Yes, not to the gate.
screens.why5: 'By hand' hints that some tool could do it for me, so a bit of the product's angle leaks into a question that should only ask about the chore.
screens.why6: It's short, one question, and ends with 'Yes or no', so I'd hear it once and answer.
screens.why7: The gate is a sound Yes/No on one act inside the window with no escape, but 'by hand' is the card's listed pitfall of hinting at another way, and nearly every super who attaches photos goes through them, so the event leans toward the routine and leaves No to few.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you go back through your walk photos to fill in the daily log? Yes · No

screens.why1: I just said yes to sorting photos by hand this week, so asking on how many of those days is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: Going through the day's site photos and picking what goes in the daily log is my evening, so I get it on one read.
screens.why3: I know which of the last five days I sat in the trailer going through photos for the log, so I can count it straight.
screens.why4: One button per working day from 1 to 5 covers every true answer for someone who already said yes, with no overlap, and *I can't recall* fits.
screens.why5: It asks about my own photos and my log, and nothing of anybody's product reaches me beyond the *by hand* I already heard at the gate.
screens.why6: It is short, has one question and one clear count to say back, and the escape comes last, so I can answer it heard once.
screens.why7: It names the unit once in the window phrase, the 8-word clause is an act done on a given day, it shows buttons 1 to 5 with no zero and only the *I can't recall* escape, and a founder low of 2 or more lets the lower buttons count against.

screens.why1: Right after asking how many days I sorted photos by hand, asking which of my after-walk chores I'd most want easier makes obvious sense.
screens.why2: RFIs, subs, the schedule, the walk and the daily log are all my everyday words, and I can answer on one read.
screens.why3: Every one of these is something I do myself after a site walk, so I can pick from what I actually did this week.
screens.why4: The other four are distinct and real, but 'Logging the day's photos and notes' is basically the whole daily log, not the sorting-photos-by-hand pain I was just asked about, so it soaks up picks for the wrong reason.
screens.why5: Nothing about the product leaks, but the hurt I was asked about, sorting site photos by hand, has widened into logging photos and notes in general, which drifts from what the founder is testing.
screens.why6: It's one short question with five short, parallel options and one escape at the end, easy to hold when heard once.
screens.why7: The own row is on the list and not first, there are four rivals, and 'None of these' is the escape, but the own row restates the circumstance (getting photos and notes into the log) instead of the hurt on its verb (sorting photos by hand), which the card forbids.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. Which one of these would you most like made easier? Writing up RFIs for issues found on the walk · Updating the schedule after the walk · Following up on safety issues from the walk · Lining up subs to show up tomorrow · Sorting the day's site photos by hand for the log · None of these

screens.why1: The last screen had me think of my last daily log, so asking how writing it up went is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: I walk the site several times a day, so 'the site walk' makes me stop and work out which one they mean, probably the last walk before I write the log.
screens.why3: I write the daily log every day and know roughly how long it took me last time.
screens.why4: The times leave gaps and overlap: an hour and a half fits nowhere, 'a couple of hours' runs into 'the rest of the evening', 'in the trailer' fails if I did it at home in an hour, and a log I fill in through the day doesn't fit 'typed up after the walk'; 'Someone else did it' fits, since the assistant super or project engineer sometimes writes it.
screens.why5: Nothing about any product or the founder's terms comes through; it's just my log and my time.
screens.why6: One short question and five short options I can keep in my head when it's read out, with the escape said last.
screens.why7: Every rung is on one measure, time to get the log written; the first rung is the log done fast, the last is never written up, the order runs best to worst, and the one escape fits a job that can be handed off.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. How long did writing it up take after your last walk of the day? Under half an hour; half an hour to an hour; one to two hours; more than two hours; or it didn't get done that day. Or say someone else did it.
